prompt: Output exactly one literal, factual sentence (8–16 words) describing only visible content in the image. Do not add labels, examples, lists, or extra text. Structure the sentence as: Primary subject (noun) + at least one high‑signal attribute + action/pose and, if visible, a short spatial/location phrase or nearby object. Place at least one high‑signal token within the first five words; include a second high‑signal token when it is clearly visible. High‑signal tokens = specific object class (e.g., electric guitar, fountain), visible color or pattern, clear count, clothing/accessory, or legible text/logo (include exact text verbatim). Keep attribute immediately before the noun (e.g., “red bicycle,” not “bicycle that is red”); short compound attributes or hyphenation (e.g., “dark-blue jacket,” “red-and-white flag”) are allowed when both attributes are visible. Prefer specific nouns (saxophone, motorbike, banner) over generic terms. Use present‑participle verbs for visible actions (riding, holding, standing). If a distinct nearby object or surface is visible, include a short spatial token (next to, on, in front of, near) to link them. Use Arabic numerals when each item is fully visible and separable; if more than three or indistinct use “several”; if uncertain, omit counts. Use “person” when gender/age/role is unclear; use “man,” “woman,” or “child” only when clearly visible. Do not infer unseen attributes (age, emotion, intent, relationships) and avoid figurative or subjective language. Output exactly one short sentence only — no extra text.
